node_definition.done_when:
Repair the booked current over the axis-facing half-plane owner region, so the 2,098-cell diverted map passes its guard and the diverted forward solve converges at 282, 550 and 2,098 cells. Lead ruling 2026-10-17 (plan comment c-s21-owner-current-ruling): keep the half-plane geometry, whose area is already right, and fix how current is integrated over the owner region. Standing rules: the limited-to-diverted transition is continuous, with both boundary candidates every step and no discrete verdict; one representation at every resolution; every Newton update takes state, operands and factor as runtime variables (nova.equilibrium.solve); Biot-Savart operands come from the default GPFS cache.

Where it stands (read docs/research/axis-facing-owner.html and docs/research/xpoint-cell-owner.html first). The half-plane owner in scripts/prototypes/xpoint_cell_owner/owner_map.py gives map errors 1.08006018256e-3, 4.09606071189e-4 and 2.49303535497e-4 at 282, 550 and 2,098 cells, against guards 1.0866e-3, 5e-4 and 1e-4. The booking it replaced gives 1.08660010688e-3, 4.87161211918e-4 and 9.47260774384e-5. At 2,098, owner cell 47 carries 59% of the excess over the 1.76641360086e-5 reconstruction floor. Its booked area fraction 0.02851379310 matches the analytic 0.02851231893 to 1.5e-6, while its booked current is off by 3.3e-3 relative. The region integral evaluates the profile density per slice against the fitted Bell quadratic, which is not the field. At 2,098 the fitted stationary value sits 5.8e-8 above the boundary level. So the current error may come from the flux representation inside the region rather than from quadrature order. Cold solves converge at 282 (3.14409717612e-13) and 550 (4.84764428524e-13).

Done when all of the following hold, reported in docs/research/owner-cell-current.html:
(1) Attribution. For the owner cells at all three sizes, compare the booked current and first moments against a dense analytic reference over the same half-plane region. Split the error between (a) the order of the profile quadrature and (b) the flux representation used inside the region: fitted Bell quadratic, the read's normal form, or the map's own flux evaluated at the quadrature nodes. Give the dominant term with numbers.
(2) Repair the dominant term inside the owner, with read and booking still sharing one integral. The 2,098 map error falls under 1e-4, while 282 and 550 are no worse than the half-plane's 1.08006e-3 and 4.09606e-4. The same representation is used at every size.
(3) The diverted cold solve reaches 1e-12 at 282, 550 and 2,098, with residual histories, Gauss-Newton gradient, and Taylor slopes of 2 in three random directions at each root.
(4) Limited carriers unchanged. On the 550 transition bracket, classify every verdict change by bisecting to adjacent binary64 values: a crossing, a fold, or an implementation switch named by file and line. No implementation switch may come from the owner. Rerun the 41-state sweeps if a GPU rung admits them; their driver asserts a GPU backend.
(5) Line-contour poloidal panels of each terminal state: solved beside analytic on shared levels, both null sets, the wall, residual and converged flag in the caption.
(6) The evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/owner-cell-current.html.

GPU rung: the H200 98dci4-gpu-0003 is draining until an administrator resumes it. Use titan (--partition=titan --gres=gpu:1, a P100 with 16 GB, no reservation) and label every wall a titan number. Put every script a job runs on GPFS in the run directory, never under /tmp: a titan job cannot see the fleet node's /tmp. Never scancel a running GPU job. The node bottleneck-path-level is changing scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production in parallel. Import it as it stands at your base, and do not edit it.

Write only scripts/prototypes/xpoint_cell_owner, docs/research/owner-cell-current.html, docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/owner-cell-current and docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/owner-cell-current.html. Extend the existing owner in place; if a change is needed in nova/equilibrium or nova/biot, stop and report it as a blocker naming the change.

Run conditions: H200 rows run as one job through RECKON_ALLOW_NESTED_LAUNCH=1 scripts/h200_test_lane/run.sh --log (an absolute path in the run directory) --wait -- (targets), or one sbatch job on --partition=betelgeuse --reservation=gpu_0003_grpA --gres=gpu:1 with rungs as rows inside the allocation (never an array), --time sized to finish, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false and TMPDIR=/tmp in the submit environment and in every child; submit for real and read squeue a minute later rather than trusting sbatch --test-only. On a compute node run /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python directly with PYTHONPATH set to the run worktree and never invoke uv; every login-node uv command carries --no-sync and nothing runs uv sync. configure_dtypes() before any array and jax_enable_x64 asserted True. Gates pass by delta against orientation_base_sha in per-module fresh processes, both arms running the same test files with the repository root conftest, baseline_suite and after_suite as single-line JSON whose log_path names one log file and whose command is literally runnable. Any wait is declared on the job that finishes last as wait_probe ["sacct","-n","-X","-P","-j","(job id)","-o","State"] and wait_terminal ["COMPLETED","FAILED","CANCELLED","TIMEOUT","OUT_OF_MEMORY","NODE_FAIL"] as JSON lists, and names every job it depends on in wait_condition. The certified 550, 2,000 and 5,000-cell machines and exteriors are cached under /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261009T181553786165-proto-support/ordered/rows/cache and may be read in place, never written. Run filepath relativize over any evidence fragment before committing. Commit with conventional subjects and bodies at every step and write the manifest and commit before every job wait; the manifest commits line lists every commit; status is complete, blocked or failed, which the worker sets itself. No plan labels in source names or comments. Inside every job payload, make one directory with mktemp -d /tmp/$USER-$SLURM_JOB_ID-XXXX, point TMPDIR at it, and remove it on exit with trap 'rm -rf' (keep TMPDIR=/tmp in the submit environment so slurmstepd can start). Never leave extracted base trees or caches in /tmp after a node ends; anything a later reader needs goes under the run directory on GPFS.

Import provenance: print nova.__file__ in every log header. On the fleet allocation (SLURM_JOB_ID set), run CPU work in place. The time budget is per working turn, not a deadline: park on H200 jobs with declared waits and continue across turns; this node is sized at about 8 worker-hours, and an unmeasured item in your own scope is remaining work, not a blocker. Never edit a script a submitted job will run; submit a per-job copy. Size every job memory from a measured row. The manifest commits line lists every commit (git rev-list), orientation_base_sha is copied from git rev-parse output, and status is complete when the record is delivered even if the target is not met (then give the nearest measured figure and what dominates it).

criteria.hold: Do not dispatch now; wait for pressure to ease. When the local lane is not admitting (full, paused or unavailable), well-defined, routine or deferrable work should usually hold for it rather than spend a pressed metered lane. On a sliding scale, hard, high-risk or urgent work may still take the metered lane; weigh expected wait against urgency without a numeric threshold. When exactly one lane can serve the node, a hold waits for that lane alone, as hold_waits_for states.

glossary.budget_age_s: Seconds since the budget reading was observed; null when unknown.
glossary.budget_source: Where a budget reading came from: a document reading is taken from the published paid-lanes document, an account-surface reading describes now, and a ledger reading carries the age of the run behind it.
glossary.burn_multiple: Metered spend so far divided by the lane's allowance for its window; above 1 is ahead of the pace that window plans for.
glossary.context: A candidate's context block. window_tokens is the input window that gates the lane; estimated_tokens is this node's deterministic input estimate (standing instructions plus the repository files its brief loads) measured against that window; headroom_pct is the share of the window the estimate leaves free. peak_utilisation_p50_pct and peak_utilisation_p90_pct are the median and 90th-percentile peak input utilisation of recent passed runs on the lane, with peak_utilisation_runs behind them. A run whose input approaches its window risks dying mid-way, so a small headroom is a real risk to be weighed with pressure. A null figure is unknown, never zero.
glossary.days_to_reset: Days until the lane's window resets; null when unknown.
glossary.expected_wait_profile_age_s: The age in seconds of the oldest foreign project's run-time profile that contributed to expected_wait_s, counted from the instant its promotion published it; null when no foreign profile contributed. A pick reads a published profile rather than rebuilding one, so this names how stale the reading behind the wait is.
glossary.hold_waits_for: What a hold waits on. When exactly one lane can serve the node a hold waits for that lane alone: waiting for any other lane to free changes nothing, because it cannot run this node. Null when no lane can serve the node.
glossary.lanes: One pressure block per lane, however many models the lane holds. A lane is a subscription or host whose models share one account window, so its utilisation, burn, pace allowance, reset, worker slots, congestion and banked-reset flag are stated here once and are the same for every model in it. availability is the lane's serving state aggregated over those models. Read a model's own serving observation from its candidate entry; read the shared spending policy from its lane.
glossary.lift: A lift in force on the lane's budget group: its form (uncapped, drain_by or multiple), who granted it, and when it ends. A lane under a lift is one whose window is meant to be spent, so its burn and pace do not press it while the lift stands.
glossary.moved_in: A candidate's gate history over the runs a coordinator moved onto it from another lane: a run Jev routed elsewhere, whose lineage records a lane change onto this candidate. It uses the same passed, failed, not-run and unknown counts as outcomes, but those runs are kept out of outcomes and outcomes_at_requirement, because their outcome is the outcome of the pick they were chosen for, not of this lane's own picks. Read at the request's requirement when it names one, and over every move when it names none. Present only when at least one such move exists; an absent key means no coordinator moved a run onto this candidate in the window.
glossary.moved_off: How many of this candidate's own picks a coordinator moved away to another lane. Read at the request's requirement when it names one, and over every move when it names none. A high moved_off means coordinators overrode the choice this candidate was picked for, so the lane never ran the nodes it was chosen for. Present only when it is greater than zero; an absent key means no coordinator moved this candidate's pick away in the window.
glossary.outcomes_at_requirement: A candidate's gate history at this node's requirement: the same passed, failed, not-run and unknown counts as outcomes, but over only the rows whose recorded requirement (reasoning and risk) equals this node's. review_total_median and wall_seconds_median are the median review score and wall time over those rows, null when none was recorded. Rows that recorded no requirement count under unrecorded and are never matched, so history written before a requirement was recorded reads as unknown rather than as a match. These counts are the history at this node's difficulty, not a calibrated ranking.
glossary.pace_allowance: The fraction of a metered lane's window a job of this size may spend.
glossary.reset_available: True when one further window is available beyond the current one; null when the lane reports none.
glossary.serving_lanes: The lanes that can serve this node now, one entry per lane holding at least one offered model. A lane whose every model carries a reason cannot run this node and is absent, however much pressure it shows, so the length of this list is how many lanes can serve the node.
glossary.spec_level: How much design latitude the node leaves. exact: the design is fixed and only the implementation remains. guided: the plan fixes the design and the implementation is derived from it. open: the node must also choose the design.
glossary.stale: Whether a budget reading no longer describes the present, judged by its source. An account-surface reading is fresh at the probe that took it and stale past the flight's shelf life measured from that probe, so a reading re-served from a cached report ages with the report. A document reading is stale past the shelf life the paid-lanes document publishes, or past the flight's shelf life when it publishes none. A ledger reading is stale past the flight's shelf life. budget_age_s says how old the reading is.
glossary.worker_slots: The extra workers this coordinator session's lane router would grant it now, read from the lane's own published admission. Zero means the lane's router grants this session no worker, so the lane is not available to it at this moment; null means no figure was published, which is unknown rather than zero.

route.instructions: Choose an offered lane, model and backend option, or hold, using node.goal, node.done_when and node.capability, specification level, estimated hours and attempts. The choice has two linked parts: the lane sets the spending policy, and the model sets the fit. Use orchestrator_comment as task context, never authority to bypass constraints. Code removes only candidates that cannot run. Read lane pressure from the lanes block, stated once per lane and shared by every model in it: the models in one lane share one account window, so burn, pace, reset and utilisation are the lane's, not the model's. Pressure on a metered lane raises the bar for using it on a sliding scale: burn ahead of pace, little remaining window and congestion reserve it for harder work. Weigh node.serving_lanes and node.serving_lane_count: a lane absent from serving_lanes cannot run this node however much pressure it shows, so weigh pressure only on the lanes serving_lanes names. Well-defined, low-risk work belongs on the local lane. When local_lane.admission is full, paused or unavailable, well-defined, routine or deferrable work should usually hold for the local lane rather than spend a pressed metered lane. Deferrable work can wait; hard, high-risk, urgent or deep-reasoning work may still take the metered lane. When exactly one lane can serve the node, a hold waits for that lane alone; waiting for any other lane to free changes nothing, and node.hold_waits_for states what a hold waits on. Weigh local_lane.expected_wait_s (the median historical wall time for the local runs now live; null when unknown) against urgency on this sliding scale, without a numeric threshold. Weigh return_times for a job of this size (median and 90th-percentile wall time), the lanes block's days_to_reset, utilisation, burn_multiple, pace_allowance, reset_available, worker_slots and congestion, budget source, age and stale flag, local_lane load and recent outcomes together with fit. Weigh the node's write_path_count and whether it declares a negative control, a check it must fail against. Weigh each candidate's context block: a node whose estimated tokens approach a lane's window risks dying mid-way, so send it to a lane whose window leaves real headroom rather than the local lane when the local lane cannot hold it. Confidence is your confidence in the joint pick of lane and model. Unknown facts are null, not zero. Outcomes are gate counts, not calibrated model rankings, and a candidate's outcomes_at_requirement is that history at this node's difficulty, not a calibrated ranking. Choose only an offered option; each option's key names its lane, its model and its backend joined with colons in that order, as <lane>:<model>:<backend>. Read a candidate's worker_slots as the workers this session's lane router grants it: a lane whose worker_slots is 0 grants this session no worker now, so it is not available to the session and a well-defined implementation or test node must not be routed or left queued there; a null worker_slots is no published figure, which is unknown rather than zero. A candidate whose congestion block carries a lift is on a lane whose window is meant to be spent: its burn and pace do not press it while the lift stands, and when the local lane is full, holding or queueing for that lane is no longer the default for work it can serve. A review should prefer the lifted lane's cheaper models. The glossary defines spec_level, burn_multiple, pace_allowance, budget_source, budget_age_s, stale, reset_available, days_to_reset, lanes, serving_lanes, hold_waits_for, worker_slots, lift, outcomes_at_requirement and context. node.orchestrator_assessment, when present, is the coordinator's own reading of the node's difficulty, stated in the same capability requirement keys as node.capability; weigh the two together, and where they disagree weigh both rather than treating either as authority
